regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% looks like acceleration — up from 7.4% prior — but IIP overall printed 6.7%, down from 8.8%, and core sector slipped to 5.4% from 6.0%. The PMI composite at 54.6 flatters: manufacturing sub-index fell to 52.8 from 53.5 while services carried the headline. Quality of growth is skewing toward services and financial intermediation, not the goods-producing economy that employs the informal majority — a divergence that GDP aggregation will paper over until it can't.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% sits at only the 41st percentile, but that number is doing heavy lifting to conceal a structural fault line: fuel inflation at 22.93% — 95th percentile, up from 20.05% — is the real story, while core CPI at 3.9% (28th percentile) confirms demand-side pricing power is absent. The inversion that matters: RBI's own inflation forecast just jumped to 5.1% from 4.6%, a 50bps revision that signals the MPC sees the fuel pass-through risk even as the repo rate sits unmoved at 5.25%. If Brent holds above $100, the 2-quarter CPI lag means the February 2027 print is already partially written.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — has pushed the CD ratio to 81.4%, still at the 75th percentile despite a marginal dip from 82.5%. NBFC credit growth accelerated sharply to 14.9% from 10.6%, signalling that wholesale funding channels are being stretched to fill the deposit gap. The last time India's CD ratio sustained above 80% during a rate-pause cycle was FY14; within four quarters, the taper tantrum forced emergency tightening. Today's FX reserves are larger, but the structural funding mismatch is identical — and the regulator's risk-weight toolkit is already loaded.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% is unchanged, but the real rate calculus is shifting: with CPI at 4.45% and RBI's own forecast now at 5.1%, the ex-ante real rate is barely 15bps — insufficient to anchor inflation expectations if fuel pass-through broadens. A rate cut is not priced for the near term, and correctly so; the question is whether the next move is a hike. For housing, the average home loan rate at 7.75% (down from 8.92%) is providing affordability relief, but INR depreciation and imported inflation could reverse that transmission faster than the MPC's quarterly review cycle.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up 180bps from 75.6% — is the most credible signal in today's data set. At 74th percentile utilisation, India is entering the zone where private capex announcements historically convert to actual orders within 2-3 quarters. Commercial vehicle sales at 16.88% and two-wheeler sales at 19.7% corroborate goods movement and rural income recovery. The inversion: core sector growth slipped to 5.4% from 6.0%, meaning the capex signal is coming from downstream manufacturing, not the upstream infrastructure inputs that would confirm a durable cycle.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 crore — 71st percentile — is a strong print, but the YTD cumulative at the 14th percentile suggests the monthly beat is partly base-effect and advance-filing seasonality rather than a clean demand surge. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% and two-wheelers at 19.7% confirm that both urban discretionary and rural aspirational demand are holding. The tension: credit card growth has decelerated sharply to 2.3% from 5.6%, which either signals consumer balance sheet prudence or early stress in the unsecured segment — the two readings have very different implications for consumption durability over the next two quarters.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 350bps divergence widening for three consecutive months. CD ratio at 81.4% (down from 82.5% prior month but structurally elevated). NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY, signalling wholesale funding pressure. Credit-to-deposit gap now at 10-year 75th percentile.","implication":"RBI will face mounting pressure to either tighten liquidity or signal rate cuts to stabilize deposit flows. Banks with CASA ratios below 40% and NBFCs dependent on wholesale funding (>30% of liabilities) face margin compression and funding stress. Overweight private banks with CASA >45% and strong deposit franchises (HDFC Bank, Kotak). Underweight pure-play NBFCs and smaller PSU banks reliant on bulk deposits.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at this level preceded the 2018-19 liquidity crisis and the 2022 deposit flight. Historically, when CD exceeds 80% for 3+ months, RBI intervenes within 6-8 weeks.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up 180bps from 75.6% prior month). Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY. Capex-sensitive segments (2W at 19.7%, CV at 16.88%, PV at 16%) all in double digits. Capacity utilisation now at 10-year 74th percentile — the sweet spot for fresh capex announcements.","implication":"This is the inflection point. Corporates are moving from cost-cutting to growth capex. Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Timken, Rane), cement (Ultratech, Ambuja), and industrial automation. Expect order book upgrades in Q4 FY26 results. Infrastructure plays (Larsen & Toubro, Godrej & Boyce) should see margin expansion as utilisation gains translate to pricing power.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77%+ has historically preceded 18-24 months of sustained capex growth. Last time we saw this confluence was 2016-17, which drove a 3-year bull run in capex stocks.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Retail Equity Inflows Hit All-Time High","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (Mar 2026), rising for two consecutive months from ₹29,845 Cr. SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (10-year 93rd percentile), up from ₹16.64 Tr six months ago. MF AUM at ₹87.08 Tr (86th percentile). DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr — the highest on record, rising two months in a row. SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (82nd percentile).","implication":"Domestic retail is in full accumulation mode. This is structural bid under Indian equities. Maintain overweight on mid-cap and small-cap indices — SIP money flows disproportionately into these segments. Avoid value traps in large-cap; SIP flows are momentum-driven and will chase quality. Expect sustained inflows through FY27 unless equity markets correct >15% sharply.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 93rd percentile has only been exceeded in the 2021 bull market peak. However, unlike 2021, SIP account growth (14% YoY) is moderating while AUM growth (40%+) is accelerating — a sign of ticket size expansion into affluent segments, not mass retail saturation.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (Mar 2026), up from 20.05% prior month — at 10-year 95th percentile. Brent crude at $103.07/bbl (72nd percentile), WTI at $104.37/bbl (85th percentile). Food inflation at 5.52% YoY, also rising. Headline CPI at 4.45% (41st percentile) but core CPI at 3.9% (28th percentile) — inflation is commodity-driven, not demand-driven.","implication":"RBI's inflation forecast of 5.1% is at risk of being breached if oil stays above $100/bbl. This constrains rate-cut optionality through Q2 FY27. Hedge India's oil import bill exposure — consider long INR positions or reduce exposure to oil-sensitive sectors (airlines, logistics, fertilisers). Overweight sectors with pricing power (FMCG, pharma, IT services) that can pass through cost inflation.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile last occurred in 2022 (Russia-Ukraine shock) and 2008 (pre-GFC). Both periods saw RBI hold rates despite growth concerns, creating policy lag risk.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"US Rates Sticky, Carry Trades Unwind Risk","data_text":"US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% (90th percentile), up 4 of last 5 months from 4.73%. Fed funds at 3.63% (flat, 67th percentile). BOJ rate at 1.0% (86th percentile, up from 0.75%), signalling end of ultra-loose policy. US core CPI at 2.45% (falling 2 in a row), but Fed holding steady — policy is restrictive relative to inflation. DXY at 99.58 (48th percentile, flat).","implication":"The carry trade unwind risk is real. Higher US rates + BOJ tightening = yen strength, which forces deleveraging of yen-funded positions. India is a major beneficiary of carry trades (FII inflows at 83rd percentile). A sharp yen rally could trigger a 5-10% correction in Indian equities. Reduce leverage, hedge FX exposure, and avoid illiquid small-caps. Maintain cash buffer for opportunities.","pct_10y":90,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 90th percentile with Fed on pause is a rare regime — last seen in 2018 (pre-Powell pivot). That ended with a 20% equity correction. BOJ tightening is the new variable; yen carry unwinds have historically triggered 2-3 week volatility spikes.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakening Despite Strong Inflows","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 (91st percentile, up from 95.24 two months ago). Despite FII equity inflows at ₹29,631 Cr (83rd percentile) and DII at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile), rupee is weakening. This suggests RBI is intervening to prevent sharper depreciation. Brent crude at $103/bbl is adding to import pressure. India's current account deficit risk is rising.","implication":"RBI's FX reserves are being deployed to defend the rupee — unsustainable if oil stays elevated and FII flows reverse. Expect RBI to signal INR weakness tolerance in next policy review. Overweight exporters (IT, pharma, textiles) who benefit from rupee depreciation. Avoid import-heavy sectors (auto, capital goods) unless they have strong pricing power. Consider hedging INR exposure for foreign currency liabilities.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile weakness with strong inflows is a policy signal — RBI is allowing depreciation to support exports and manage inflation. Last time this occurred (2013), rupee fell another 8% over 6 months before stabilizing.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Decoupling From IT Stocks","data_text":"Office absorption at 29.9 mn sqft (24th percentile, down from 86mn sqft implied by historical averages), while Nifty IT is flat YTD and office vacancy at 13.9% (38th percentile). Yet GCC (Global Capability Centre) leasing is accelerating — non-IT corporates (BFSI, manufacturing, consulting) are the primary absorbers. Rent in Bengaluru at ₹100.6/sqft (57th percentile) and Mumbai at ₹125/sqft (38th percentile) — both rising despite weak IT demand.","implication":"Commercial real estate is decoupling from the IT services proxy. GCCs are structural, not cyclical — they're not cutting space when IT services slow. This means office REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) are mispriced relative to their GCC exposure. Overweight office REITs; underweight pure-play IT services stocks. The narrative that 'IT weakness = office weakness' is false. Falsifiable test: If GCC leasing slows in next 2 quarters, this thesis breaks.","pct_10y":24,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 24th percentile is historically low, but the composition has shifted. GCC leasing now represents 35-40% of new absorption vs 15% five years ago. This structural shift means traditional IT-office correlation has broken.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP growth with a 7.7% full-year estimate sounds like a clean acceleration — until IIP at 6.7% (down from 8.8%) and core sector at 5.4% (down from 6.0%) reveal that goods-economy momentum is actually fading beneath the headline. PMI composite at 54.6 is at the 83rd percentile, but manufacturing slipped to 52.8 — the services sector is carrying a number that the formal goods economy isn't confirming. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% and IIP capital goods at 16.1% are the genuine bright spots: at the 74th percentile utilisation threshold, private capex announcements historically follow within two to three quarters. The risk is that fuel inflation at 22.93% — 95th percentile — compresses corporate margins before that capex cycle fully ignites.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US 10Y at 4.96% — 90th percentile, up four of the last five months — is the single most important external variable for India today, repricing EM carry trades and widening the interest rate differential that determines FII behaviour. US GDP SAAR has slowed to 1.5% from 2.1%, yet the Fed holds at 3.63% with core PCE at 3.34% — policy is restrictive relative to growth, not just inflation. The BOJ at 1.0% (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) is unwinding the last pillar of global liquidity suppression — yen carry unwind risk is not priced in India's 8th-percentile VIX at 13.4. China's composite PMI at 49.5 with GDP at 4.3% (down from 5.0%) removes the commodity demand tailwind that India's export sector was quietly relying on.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII equity net at ₹58,502 crore — an all-time high, 100th percentile — is absorbing every wave of FII hesitation, with SIP inflows at ₹32,297 crore rising for two consecutive months and SIP AUM at ₹18.62 trillion (93rd percentile). Domestic liquidity is structurally deep, but the banking system's funding architecture is under stress: credit at 17.1% against deposits at 10.8% — a 630bps gap — means banks are competing for the same retail savings that are flowing into mutual funds, creating a structural deposit-mobilisation problem that SIP growth actively worsens. NBFC credit growth jumping to 14.9% from 10.6% signals wholesale funding channels are being stretched; corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 crore sits at the 0th percentile, meaning the capital market is not providing the relief valve it should. The CD ratio at 81.4% — 75th percentile — is the number the RBI watches before reaching for macro-prudential tools.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Nifty at 23,119 (74th percentile) and Bank Nifty at 55,795 (92nd percentile) are diverging in a way that should concern equity allocators: Bank Nifty's 92nd-percentile valuation sits atop a funding structure — CD ratio at 81.4%, deposit growth at 10.8% — that historically precedes NIM compression and risk-weight tightening. India VIX at 13.4 (8th percentile) prices near-zero tail risk even as US VIX has climbed to 17.6 (12th percentile) over three of the last five sessions — the complacency gap between domestic and global volatility pricing is 9 percentile points and widening. On real estate, the GCC-led office absorption story at 29.9 mn sqft is structurally sound — non-IT corporates in BFSI and manufacturing are the primary demand source — but REIT prices tell a different story: Embassy down 16%, Mindspace down 30%, Brookfield down 21% from prior levels, suggesting the listed market is discounting a rate-for-longer scenario that the physical leasing market hasn't yet absorbed. Credit card growth at 2.3% (down from 5.6%) is the early-warning indicator for consumer discretionary earnings — watch it.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Ranked by probability × impact: first, INR at 96.15 (91st percentile) weakening despite record DII inflows confirms that Brent at $103/bbl is overwhelming the capital account — every $10 sustained on crude adds approximately $15bn to the annual import bill, widens CAD by ~40bps, and feeds back into CPI with a two-quarter lag that the RBI's 5.1% forecast may still be underestimating. Second, US 10Y at 4.96% — if it breaches 5.0%, the historical precedent from Q3 2023 is a sharp EM equity outflow episode; India's FII equity position at ₹29,631 crore net inflow could reverse faster than the DII absorption capacity can offset. Third, the CD ratio at 81.4% with NBFC credit accelerating to 14.9% creates the conditions for a macro-prudential response — risk-weight increases on unsecured lending or NBFC funding norms — that would hit consumption credit and Bank Nifty earnings simultaneously. Fourth, BOJ at 1.0% and rising is the underpriced global risk: yen carry unwind episodes have historically correlated with sharp INR depreciation and India VIX spikes within 4-6 weeks. Watch the US 10Y print this week — a 5.0% close is the single data point that changes the risk calculus for every other variable on this list.

"}
